First proper trip here, 5 to 8 October 2023, with Leonor and Dani. The weekend that made me move to Lisbon eight
months later. Keeping the note as-is because past me was adorably clueless.

## Where we stayed

Airbnb in Graça, Travessa do Monte 31, 3rd floor, no lift. €96 a night for three nights, split three ways. Booking
ref LSB-2310-77. Tiny balcony with a view of the castle, washing machine that sounded like a jet engine.

## Day 1: Alfama and the miradouros

Tram 28 queue at Martim Moniz was 50 minutes, so we walked. Best decision of the trip. Miradouro da Senhora do Monte
at sunset, then down through Alfama, completely lost twice. Dinner at Tasca da Rosinha: bacalhau à brás €12.50,
house wine €2 a glass, grilled sardines for Dani.

## Day 2: Belém

Pastéis de Belém, queue 25 minutes, six for €7.80, ate four on the spot. Jerónimos monastery €12, cloister is
unreal. Walked along the river to the Padrão dos Descobrimentos. Feet destroyed by 4pm.

## Day 3: Sintra

Train from Rossio, €2.40 each way, about 40 minutes. Pena Palace ticket €20 including the park. Quinta da Regaleira
for the initiation well, which had a 30 minute line on a Saturday. Mistake: going on a Saturday at all. Next time a
Tuesday and the 8:41 train.

## Fado night

"A Voz da Graça", small room, minimum spend €25 each. Singer named Celeste Amaral, maybe 60, made Leonor cry during
the second song. No phones allowed during the songs and honestly that made it.

## Getting around

Viva Viagem card €0.50, then load it with "zapping" credit, €1.61 a ride. The calçada stones are like ice when wet:
wear shoes with grip. The hills are no joke, Graça to Baixa is fine, the way back up is a workout.

## Things I'd do differently

- Skip tram 28 entirely, take the 12E or just walk
- Book Sintra tickets online the day before
- Sort travel insurance before booking, not the night before, see [[Travel insurance comparison]]
- Bring fewer clothes; I packed from [[Packing list carry-on]] and still overdid it

## Portuguese I picked up

"Obrigada" (I'm a woman, so -a), "uma bica" for an espresso, "a conta, se faz favor". Nobody minded my Spanish
accent but they all switched to English instantly. That's what pushed me into tandem meetups once I moved, notes in
[[Language exchange partners]].
